free_text: The 64-year-old male presents with an elevated PSA of 7.8 ng/mL and a prostate cancer diagnosis of clinically T1c, Grade Group 2 (4+3), ISUP grade group 2. The mpMRI showed a suspicious focal lesion (PI-RADS 4). Given the established low-risk pathological grade and the mild LUTS (IPSS 1/35), the management assessment focuses on individual treatment benefit and patient preferences.
